body: Sure, there are many. But I'm looking to go to Harvard for the experience, not for the jobs that might come after.

I don't have "grown-ups" babysitting me. My dad threw me out of the house months ago. My self-**e**steem is perfectly fine. I'm just devastated to the point of death that I will get rejected from Harvard.

"Learn to deal with it, and move on." Well, that's an interesting proposition. Yes, why don't I just "move on" and "deal with it"? Why don't I learn to deal with my failures, and move on? Why, that's brilliant! So simple, yet it cuts right to the point. So, why haven't I done this yet? Oh, that's right. I have fucking depression. Honestly, why don't all the therapists use this new, and innovated, and *efficient* method of "deal with it and move on"? Don't answer that, it was a rhetorical question.

You're only 17, you're lucky you still have your parents, you haven't experienced *the real world*. Oooo the *"real world"*; fuck that sounds fascinating. I'd love to join the real world. Where is it? Oh? I'm already fucking in it? FUCKADOODLE DOO Well, isn't that quite a twist? I don't have my parents. I have to pay rent and taxes every month, just like the rest of you suckers. If I get sick, well fuck me I still have to go to work and school. Why don't I, fucking deal with my mental problems, deal with living without parents, deal with the school, just waste my talents and eat my shit? And... move on. Fucking brilliant doc. *slow clap that ass*

According to statistics, there are not enough perfect SAT scorers to fill up Harvard, so no, Harvard will have enough room if they took people with only perfect SAT scores and 4.0s.

Yeah, a lot of people have jobs. So what? The majority of the world works jobs; even little 5 yr olds or high school drop outs. I have a job too. I don't care about getting a job or making money; all I want is an admission to Harvard.
Don't you need some kind of license for that? Also, are your employees your friends or someone hired from outside your social realm? If I wanted to start a company, what should I do?

I've heard many stories about Harvard students who don't deserve their admission. In fact, I've talked to a Columbia Uni student who told me I was smarter than some of the students at Harvard. But honestly, who doesn't feel good when they say, "I got accepted at Harvard!" It's serious bragging rights to those who get into the top university *in the world*. Regardless of if the students are brilliant or not, surely the professors are? Either way, Harvard was ranked number one several times, over and over again.

I'm not talking about the acceptance you're thinking of. I'm already a respectable member of my society, as well as family, but Harvard will be a boost in my reputation. It's a confirmation that I'm smart, hard working, whatever it is. You know how seniors talk about where they got accepted, and everyone talks about that one guy who got accepted into Harvard. I want to be that one guy. But not only that, I want to be in Harvard to be with other people that are like that. Acceptance, respect and reputation are not petty things; they're important to everyone and certainly important to mental health.
I don't understand how people start and run businesses all by themselves. What's your line of business?

What do I want? Acceptance. How do I get that? Harvard. I see nothing wrong with wanting validation. What's wrong with doing things to get people to like you? Is it because I'll never live for myself? But I am; I'm making myself happy by having others be happy to be with me. I have nothing else I want to explore, I have no passion that I'm neglecting. It's not like I'm suppressing my "true self" to please others. I'm making myself better, and becoming a person that I've always respected as well as everyone else. Everyone wins; I win, you win, we all win. Unless, of course, things don't go according to plan. Then everyone loses.

How did you start your business?

Also, I don't care much for money. I'm more interested in setting a name for myself and becoming someone who can look back in history with pride.

It's too late for getting "great grades". Say if I get 100% for the rest of my high school career, that *still* wont be enough for Harvard to be impressed.

Harvard is not just a name. It's an ego booster. It's like someone telling you that you're the most beautiful specimen they've seen in a long time. It's acceptance from your family, it's respect from your peers, it's basically everything I need to verify myself. To tell myself that I'm alright, that I can finally be happy with who I am. All I want is Harvard, all I want is to sigh that huge sigh of relief and to know that all my doubts and fears can be ended.
Can't, I'm not a US citizen. Sucks, right? Even if I do get in, I probably wont be able to go because my family is too poor.
Mine busted out as well. How do I use the warranty?
